units.title: Microstructure and its Relation to Properties of Refractory Materials.
topics: 1.1. Introduction to Microstructure  Definition and importance  Constituents: grains, pores, and glassy phase  Alumina-silica phase diagrams.
1.2. Factors Affecting Microstructure  Raw materials and impurities  Manufacturing process (mixing, shaping, firing)  Firing temperature, atmosphere, and cooling rate

1.3. Relation between Microstructure and Properties  Effect of grain size, porosity, and bonding on strength and density  Influence on thermal conductivity and thermal shock resistance  Relation with corrosion and slag resistance

units.title: Uses of Refractory Materials
topics: 2.1. Introduction and Classification of Uses  Importance of refractories in industries  Classification based on area of use: o Metallurgical o Non-metallurgical  Selection criteria for different applications

2.2. Uses in Metallurgical Industries  Iron and steel industry – furnaces, ladles, converters  Non-ferrous metal industry – copper, aluminium, zinc smelting furnaces  Cement, glass, and ceramic kilns

2.3. Uses in Non-Metallurgical and Special Applications  Petrochemical and chemical industries  Power generation, incinerators, and boilers  Space, nuclear, and electronic applications (advanced refractories)

units.title: Kiln Furniture
topics: 3.1. Introduction and Functions  Definition and importance of kiln furniture  Role in supporting ceramic ware during firing  Desired properties of kiln furniture (mechanical strength, thermal shock resistance, etc.)

units.title: Properties and Tests of Refractory
topics: 4.1. Physical Properties  Porosity, bulk density, and apparent specific gravity  Refractoriness and refractoriness under load (RUL)  Thermal expansion and thermal conductivity
4.2. Mechanical and Thermal Properties  Cold crushing strength (CCS) and modulus of rupture (MOR)  Thermal shock resistance and spalling behavior  Creep resistance at high temperature
4.3. Chemical and Slag Resistance Tests  Corrosion and erosion resistance tests  Methods for testing chemical stability and quality control.

units.title: Pollution Control and Safety in Refractory Industries
topics: 5.1. Sources of Pollution in Refractory Industries  Air pollution: dust, smoke, and gaseous emissions during crushing, mixing, and firing  Water and land pollution from effluents and waste materials  Noise pollution from machinery and handling equipment
5.2. Pollution Control Methods  Dust collection systems: bag filters, cyclones, scrubbers  Wastewater treatment and recycling methods  Proper disposal of solid and hazardous wastes
5.3. Industrial Safety and Health Measures  Common hazards in refractory plants (heat, dust, heavy equipment)  Safety devices and protective equipment (PPE)
